title: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book 1, Fugue 5 in D major

sections.label: Episode 1
sections.summary: Soprano: the opening of the subject (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every half bar. Alto: a figure from the subject. Tenor: the opening of the subject (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every half bar.

sections.label: Episode 2
sections.summary: Soprano: free counterpoint, in a sequence falling by a third every beat. Alto: free counterpoint. Tenor: free counterpoint. Bass: the opening of the subject. Returns in Episode 3 (bars 16–19).

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in G major (Bass); Subject in G major (Soprano)
Episode 3
sections.summary: Reworks Episode 2 (bars 9–10), with soprano and bass exchanged, the lines moved by different intervals. Soprano: the opening of the subject (3 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Alto: free counterpoint, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Tenor: a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every bar.

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in D major, rhythm varied (Soprano); Subject in D major (Alto)
Episode 4
sections.summary: Soprano: the opening of the subject (4 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and a figure from the subject, in a sequence falling by a step every half bar. Alto: free counterpoint, in a sequence falling by a fifth every half bar. Tenor: a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and the opening of the subject, in a sequence falling by a fifth every half bar. Bass: a figure from the subject (6 times) and the opening of the subject (5 times) and the opening of the subject, inverted, in a sequence rising by a fourth every beat.

spans.label: Codetta
spans.summary: Tenor: the opening of the subject. Bass: free counterpoint.
